title: Expedited partner therapy: the practitioner authority in M.G.L. c. 111, s. 121B and 105 CMR 700.003(H) and the form of the partner prescription
subtopic: Statutory and regulatory authority for expedited partner therapy and the partner prescription
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 111, s. 121B provides that, notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, the department, in consultation with the board of registration in medicine, shall promulgate regulations authorizing a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner or certified nurse midwife who is authorized under chapter 94C to prescribe and dispense prescription drugs and who diagnoses infections due to Chlamydia trachomatis and other sexually transmitted infections suitable for expedited partner treatment based on national standards, including, but not limited to, standards outlined in the Center for Disease Control's Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines and as further defined in regulation by the department, to prescribe and dispense such prescription drugs to a patient's sexual partners for the presumptive treatment of infection without an examination of the patient's sexual partners. The words concerning other sexually transmitted infections were inserted by St. 2024, c. 140, s. 113, in place of the words 'in individual patients'; section 114 of that act struck out the word 'Chlamydia' in line 9 of section 121B; and section 264 of that act provides that, except as otherwise specified, the act shall take effect on July 1, 2024. Under 105 CMR 700.003(H), notwithstanding any other provision of 105 CMR 700.000, a registered physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner, or nurse midwife may provide expedited partner therapy (EPT) for the treatment of chlamydia infection, which is the prescribing or dispensing for immediate treatment of an appropriate therapeutic agent in Schedule VI for the treatment of a sex partner or partners of a patient diagnosed with chlamydia infection, provided that: (1) the prescribing or dispensing is in accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(H), 243 CMR 2.00, 263 CMR 5.00, 244 CMR 4.00, and any applicable guidelines of the Department, the Board of Registration in Medicine, the Board of Registration of Physician Assistants, the Board of Registration in Nursing, and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; (2) in a case in which the patient is provided with a therapeutic agent for immediate treatment of the patient's sex partner, the therapeutic agent shall be provided to the patient in a separate, properly labeled container for the sex partner to be given the therapeutic agent; (3) in a case in which the patient is provided with a prescription for the patient's sex partner, there shall be a separate prescription for the sex partner, which includes on the prescription form, where the name and address of the patient is to be noted, either the name of the sex partner or the words 'Expedited Partner Therapy,' 'E.P.T.' or 'EPT'; and (4) the physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner, or nurse midwife counsels the patient about EPT and whenever possible provides the patient with an information sheet provided by the Department, or comparable to that provided by the Department, for the sex partner. The information sheet shall include pertinent information about procedures for taking the medication, avoiding sexual activity as required during treatment, possible allergic reactions, and avoiding future infection, and, as appropriate, patient counseling may also include suggested ways of notifying and providing the medication or prescription to the sex partner.
exam_relevance: Tests who may provide expedited partner therapy, for which infection the regulation provides it, what the separate partner prescription carries where the patient's name and address would be noted, and the difference between the broader statutory authorization and the chlamydia-only regulation.

authority.name: Prescription and distribution of drugs to treat Chlamydia and other sexually transmitted infections in unexamined sexual partners of patients
Acts of 2024, Chapter 140, amending section 121B of chapter 111
Expedited partner therapy for the treatment of chlamydia infection

exceptions: Where the practitioner provides the therapeutic agent itself for the sex partner, 105 CMR 700.003(H)(2) calls for a separate, properly labeled container for the sex partner rather than a partner prescription.
The Department information sheet for the sex partner is to be provided whenever possible.
common_confusions: Extending the regulation to gonorrhea or another infection because s. 121B now refers to other sexually transmitted infections; the statute leaves those infections to be further defined in regulation, and 105 CMR 700.003(H) provides expedited partner therapy for the treatment of chlamydia infection.

Listing pharmacists among the practitioners who may provide expedited partner therapy; 105 CMR 700.003(H) names a registered physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner or nurse midwife.

Treating a prescription in the index patient's name as covering the partner; where the patient is provided with a prescription for the sex partner there shall be a separate prescription for the sex partner.

Assuming the partner's address must accompany the partner's name; 105 CMR 700.003(H)(3) calls for either the name of the sex partner or one of the three designations where the name and address of the patient is to be noted.

Placing the expedited partner therapy counseling and information sheet on the pharmacist; 105 CMR 700.003(H)(4) places them on the physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner or nurse midwife.
